authored.notes:
Design choice rationale: the roadmap mandated atomicMax-of-per-step-delta (decoder semantics), so I REPLACED the existing half-built workspace-'+='-into-prof[] scaffold with a __device__ g_mb_prof_max buffer + a CTA-local __shared__ MbProf accumulator, exactly mirroring the decoder. This is why mb_tc_workspace_floats no longer carries a profiler term at all (removed the #if-gated workspace carve) — a side benefit is the ON workspace now equals the OFF workspace, so the profiler read does not enlarge the d=1024 staged-opt scratch.

The SG_MBPROF macros (TIC/ACC/PARAM/ARG/LOCAL + the kernel-side KERNEL_CLOSE helper) live in model_stage_mamba3.cuh so the device sample fns can use them; the g_mb_prof_max buffer + the kernel P1 atomicMax-of-slots-0-5 + P2/P3 brackets live in fused_mamba_megakernel.cuh. The scalar megakernel (SG_MB_SCALAR_MEGAKERNEL, the non-profiled d=128 path) and the SAM 2nd-backward (constexpr'd out of AdamW) both required SG_MBPROF_ARG to type-check when ON — they feed a throwaway/unread accumulator (documented in-code); neither is the profiled path (the bench drives tc_train_step<AdamW> -> tc_profile_read).

Slot semantics for the main loop's interpretation: each slot is the MAX-across-CTAs of that CTA's per-step phase total = the slowest-CTA critical path (what the trailing grid barrier waits on). Slots 0-5 are summed across this CTA's samples inside the sample fns then published at end-of-P1; slots 6/7 are the kernel's own P2/P3. The bench prints SCAN=slot0+1, PROJECTION=slot2+3, SURFACE=slot4+5 shares — the campaign's scan-vs-projection arbiter.

Left tuning/_mbtc_bypass_profile.py untouched (its -D flags SG_MBTC_BYPASS_SCAN/DW_GEMM/EMBED_SCAN appear nowhere in csrc/ — dead, do-not-resurrect per the roadmap).

authored.fix:
Fixed the compile.py _emitted_sources KEYING bug (Phase C0.0 latent fake-green). ROOT CAUSE: the generative emitter path (_variant_macros, behind spec.enable_emitter) stashed its rendered source under the BARE key `config_key(config)`, while build_jit's winner-swap reads the COMPOSITE key `f"{won_ckey}:synth"` (gated on _LAST_VARIANT_ORIGIN==ORIGIN_SYNTH). The keys differed, so the swap could NEVER fire for an emitter/generated winner — a generated winner would silently ship a TEMPLATE build under its validated timing (the exact #16/P0-3 false-green the gates exist to stop).

DECISION (traced BOTH call sites + all stash/read sites): made _variant_macros stash on the SAME composite key build_jit reads, because the REST of the source-swap path is already composite — the synth stash (timer) writes `<ckey>:synth`, the polyhedral stash writes `<ckey>:polyhedral`, and build_jit reads `<ckey>:synth`. The emitter's bare-key stash was the lone outlier. The emitter is the generative source path whose winner is stamped origin=ORIGIN_SYNTH (per the C0.1 design step "Stamp ORIGIN_SYNTH at the variant point"), so it correctly stashes under the synth key the swap reads.

IMPLEMENTATION (single-source-of-truth, drift-proof):
1. Added helper `_emitted_source_key(ckey, origin) -> f"{ckey}:{origin}"` (next to the ORIGIN_* constants) as the ONE place the composite key is built.
2. Routed ALL emitted-source key sites through it: _variant_macros stash (was bare config_key -> now `_emitted_source_key(config_key(config), ORIGIN_SYNTH)`), build_jit swap read, the synth stash, the polyhedral stash, AND the polyhedral feeder read (which is the ONLY consumer of the emitter's stash today — it had to move to the same composite key or the polyhedral fan-out would silently lose its input source).
3. Added a NEW behavioral self-test `emitted_source_stash_key_matches_swap_read_key`: runs the emitter, recovers the actually-stashed key, asserts it == the key build_jit reads for a synth-origin winner (computed via the same helper), asserts the BARE config_key is ABSENT (regression guard for the exact pre-fix bug), and asserts synth/polyhedral keys don't collide. Falls back to a pure contract check when jinja2 is absent.
4. Updated the existing `synth_winner_swaps_source_in_final_build` and `codegen_variant_macros_hook` self-tests to the helper-based keying (they previously asserted the now-changed bare-key/literal behavior), and bumped _SELF_TEST_EXPECTED_COUNT 231->232 for the new case.

BYTE-IDENTICAL on the real path today: no emitter/synth/polyhedral generative origin has ever won (the generative back-ends are non-functional), so the stashed value is never consumed by the swap yet — this only makes the swap CORRECT for when a generated origin wins (the #27 C0 path).

authored.notes: SUBTLETY worth the main loop's attention: the emitter's bare-key stash was NOT entirely orphaned — its sole live consumer today is the polyhedral feeder in _make_variant_timer (`(spec._emitted_sources or {}).get(ckey)`), which reads the emitted source to transform it. I moved that read to the SAME composite key, so the polyhedral fan-out keeps working (it would otherwise have silently lost its input). build_jit's swap and the synth stash already agreed on `<ckey>:synth` BEFORE this fix (so synth-origin swap was already correct) — the bug was strictly the EMITTER stash vs the swap read. Choosing ORIGIN_SYNTH for the emitter key (not a new ORIGIN_EMITTER) matches both build_jit's existing hardcoded `:synth` read AND the C0.1 design's "stamp ORIGIN_SYNTH at the variant point", and avoids touching build_jit's origin-detection branch. enable_emitter and enable_synth_codegen can both be on; in that case the synth stash (later in the timer) overwrites the emitter's `<ckey>:synth` entry with the synth source, which is the correct precedence (synth-only mode replaces template sources). All keying now flows through one helper (_emitted_source_key) so stash-key==swap-read-key by construction and the new self-test pins it against silent drift.
